\section[la marginación]{la marginación — the social exclusion, the marginalisation}

\label{lesson:ES-C605-marginacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to claim, then the Spanish for to demand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la marginación}
\textbf{la marginación} — \textquotedblleft{}the social exclusion, the marginalisation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Muchas personas viven en la marginación.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Many people live on the margins of society.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{marginar} — to push to the edge.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{marginación} is built on \emph{marginar}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{marginare} (EtymDB), from \emph{margo} 'edge, border'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la marginación}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la marginación}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la marginación}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to claim, then the Spanish for to demand, then say \emph{la marginación} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la marginación mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The social exclusion, the marginalisation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la discriminación]{la discriminación — the discrimination}

\label{lesson:ES-C605-discriminacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the social exclusion, then the Spanish for the violence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la discriminación}
\textbf{la discriminación} — \textquotedblleft{}the discrimination\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La discriminación en el trabajo va contra la ley.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Discrimination at work is against the law.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Discriminar} — to discriminate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{discriminación} is built on \emph{discriminar}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{discriminare} 'to divide', from \emph{discrimen} 'a dividing line', from \emph{cernere} 'to sift' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

Before the new one: say the Spanish for the violence, then the Spanish for the discrimination.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el racismo}
\textbf{el racismo} — \textquotedblleft{}the racism\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El racismo no tiene excusa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\emph{Racista} — racist.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{racismo} is built on \emph{raza} 'race' with \emph{-ismo}; the origin of \emph{raza} is not settled, and EtymDB traces it through Old Spanish \emph{raça} to Latin \emph{radius}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[la corrupción]{la corrupción — the corruption}

\label{lesson:ES-C605-corrupcion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the discrimination, then the Spanish for the racism.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la corrupción}
\textbf{la corrupción} — \textquotedblleft{}the corruption\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La gente está cansada de la corrupción.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{People are tired of corruption.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Corrupto} — corrupt.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{corrupción} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{corruptio} 'decay, spoiling', built on \emph{corrumpere}, from \emph{rumpere} 'to break' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
